result.title: How Many Demonstrations Does a VLA Need? On the Sample Efficiency of VLA Finetuning
result.summary: Pretrained vision language action (VLA) models show strong zero-shot performance, but are rarely deployed directly and are often first post-trained on demonstrations from the target setting. Yet VLAs are typically compared by zero-shot or full-data fine-tuned success, revealing little about the data and compute required for adaptation. We study adaptation efficiency for six VLAs ($π_{0}$, $π_{0.5}$, and GR00T N1-N1.7) on four LIBERO suites, varying both demonstrations and training steps. This reveals differences hidden by full-data fine-tuning: models within two points on the full LIBERO-Spatial dataset differ by up to $3\times$ in success with 50 demonstrations. $π_{0.5}$ needs $2$--$5\times$ fewer demonstrations than $π_{0}$ and is the most sample-efficient model at every budget, with the largest gap on the long-horizon suite. Within GR00T, N1.5 adapts more efficiently than N1.6 and N1.7 on three of four suites, despite their stronger zero-shot performance. We study one pretraining factor behind these differences by freezing the VLM during finetuning: this severely degrades the $π$ models, whose VLM is jointly trained with the action expert during pretraining, but barely affects GR00T models. Finally, validation loss on held-out demonstrations tracks closed-loop success within a suite, but understates how much more sample-efficient $π_{0.5}$ is than $π_{0}$.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在四个 LIBERO 套件上同时改变示范数量与训练步数，比较六种 VLA（π0、π0.5、GR00T N1–N1.7）的适配样本效率，并分析冻结 VLM 的影响以及验证损失与闭环成功率是否一致。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结 VLM 以归因预训练因素」和「验证损失低估适配差距」的做法，可供核查视觉表征贡献分配与代理指标能否反映 latent 推理收益；但研究对象是机器人动作适配，与 LVR 主线联系较弱。
